prompt: RFC 3986 relative-part path rule instead of path-rootless
answer:
In RFC 3986, `relative-part` uses `path-noscheme`, not `path-rootless`:

```abnf
relative-part = "//" authority path-abempty
              / path-absolute
              / path-noscheme
              / path-empty
```

By contrast, `hier-part` uses `path-rootless`:

```abnf
hier-part = "//" authority path-abempty
          / path-absolute
          / path-rootless
          / path-empty
```

The distinction is that a relative-path reference cannot have a colon (`:`) in its first path segment, because it could otherwise be interpreted as a scheme name:

```abnf
path-noscheme = segment-nz-nc *( "/" segment )
path-rootless = segment-nz *( "/" segment )
```
